title: Design a Scalable Web Crawler
subtitle: From single-threaded URL fetcher to multi-million page distributed frontier

stages.title: Stage 1 — Basic Single-Threaded Fetcher
stages.bottleneck: Infinite loops (crawling duplicate URLs), politeness violations (DDOSing target domains), memory overflow.
stages.narrative:
**Naive Web Crawler.** A script pops a URL from a list, fetches the HTML, extracts links using regex, and appends them back to the list.

**Issues:** Trapped in cyclic links (`/a -> /b -> /a`), overwhelms small web servers by firing 1,000 requests/sec to a single domain.

stages.title: Stage 2 — URL Frontier with Politeness & Priority
stages.bottleneck: Storing billions of seen URLs in RAM for deduplication causes Out-Of-Memory (OOM) crashes.
stages.narrative:
**URL Frontier & Politeness.** The Frontier uses 2 sets of queues:
1. **Priority Queues:** Rank URLs based on PageRank or refresh frequency.
2. **Politeness Queues:** Assign 1 queue per target host with a delay timer (e.g. 1s between requests to `example.com`).

stages.title: Stage 3 — Distributed Deduplication & Storage
stages.bottleneck: Duplicate content across mirrors/CDNs wastes bandwidth and storage.
stages.narrative:
**Scalable Content & Link Filtering.**
1. **Bloom Filters:** In-memory probabilistic datastructure tests whether a URL has been seen with 99.9% accuracy in sub-microsecond time.
2. **SimHash / Near-duplicate detection:** Fingerprints page text to ignore duplicate mirror sites.
